lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs are not merely losing; they are losing their grip on the opening month. Saturday's 4-1 defeat to the Islanders extended Toronto's skid to three games, leaving the club 3-4, 11th in the Eastern Conference with eight points. The warning light is flashing. Auston Matthews has called for more urgency from the top players, and the injury to John Tavares has forced Toronto to recall Marlies forward Vinni Lettieri - hardly the sort of reinforcement a contender wants this early. There was one encouraging note: Gavin McKenna responded to his benching with a season-high 17:56 and four shots, a sign Jim Hiller may finally be trusting the rookie's speed and imagination. But promise is not production. Tonight's 7:30 p.m. meeting with San Jose is the next test: beat the Sharks, or let this slow start become the season's defining story.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and the Blue Jays now face the harder part: deciding which version of this roster deserves another chance. Toronto finished 79-83 and second in the AL East, but the real warning lies in how quickly last year's formula lost its bite. Alejandro Kirk's latest contribution came from the other side of the postseason fence, advising childhood friend Jonathan Aranda to relax and be himself as Tampa Bay's run continued. Kirk remains a keeper in more ways than one - a steady catcher, a trusted voice, and one of the few Toronto players whose value extends beyond the box score. The club's next answers may come from Arizona, where prospects are making their case for 2027, while Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and four teammates remain Gold Glove finalists. Watch the prospect evaluations and the first pitching moves: Toronto needs more than a familiar type next spring - it needs a roster built to survive October.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors have finished the dress rehearsal, and the margins are already visible. The 129-125 loss to Detroit on Oct. 16 closed a 2-3 preseason - a result that matters less than the lineup Toronto chose not to show, with Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and RJ Barrett among the regulars rested. Trayce Jackson-Davis supplied 23 points, but the real work came Saturday: Toronto waived five players and converted centre Nate Bittle to a two-way contract, trimming the camp clutter before the serious accounting begins. The Raptors sit third in the Atlantic Division, 2.5 games behind, though preseason standings are decorative at best. Leonard's integration remains the headline; his expected return should clarify how Barnes and Barrett fit around him. Wednesday's 7:30 p.m. opener against Chicago is the first meaningful look at Toronto's projected rotation - and the first test of whether this rebuilt hierarchy travels beyond exhibition speed.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: A tie can reveal more than a loss, and Washington's 27-27 deadlock with the Giants exposed a team still learning how to finish. Jayden Daniels' admission that the botched final play was "ultimately" on him is the right starting point, even if the quarterback's decision to run in bounds with no timeouts erased a chance at a winning field goal. Daniels returned from his elbow injury with 302 total yards and two rushing touchdowns, but accountability matters more than numbers this morning. At 1-3-1, Washington sits second in the NFC East, 1.5 games back, carrying a one-game losing streak into a brutal test. Jacory Croskey-Merritt is out with a groin injury; Stefon Diggs remains questionable with a hamstring issue. Now comes Monday night at 8:15 p.m. ET in San Francisco, where Washington must turn Daniels' lesson into composed football against the unbeaten 49ers.

article.title: Leafs Host Sharks as Stolarz Starts
paragraphs: The Leafs bring a 3-4 record into tonight's visit from the Sharks, with Anthony Stolarz projected to start against Alex Nedeljkovic at 7:30 PM ET. Toronto is 11th in the Eastern Conference, and the focus is on finding traction after a slow start. Jim Hiller and Gavin McKenna have taken steps forward, but the losses have mounted.

The Jays are represented in Arizona Fall League action, while catcher Alejandro Kirk is advising Tampa Bay's Jonathan Aranda during the postseason. The Raptors have converted centre Nate Bittle to a two-way contract and waived five players; they open the regular season against the Bulls on Wednesday at 7:30 PM ET. The Commanders visit the 49ers at 8:15 PM ET on ESPN, with Jean-Baptiste and Omenihu out, and Diggs and Cross questionable.
